title: Senate Passes Revised Private-Property Bill as Protesters Clash With Police
detail: Thousands marched on Congress as the Senate debated Milei's 'Inviolability of Private Property' bill, which aimed to streamline evictions, restrict state expropriations, and change rural land-use rules. To secure enough votes, the government dropped the bill's most contentious provision — raising the cap on foreign purchases of rural land from 15% to 25% — after opposition from provincial governors and land-sovereignty campaigners chanting 'the homeland is not for sale.' Clashes outside Congress lasted over four hours: police used tear gas, rubber bullets, and a water cannon; at least two officers and one protester were injured, a photojournalist was struck in the head, and ten people were arrested. The Senate passed the pared-back bill later that day.
